target_description.entry_point: ConstraintExpr tree construction and evaluation from arbitrary bytes
target_description.input_format: Arbitrary bytes interpreted as constraint expression trees with field element operands
assertions: Must not panic on any input — malformed trees are rejected gracefully
Evaluation results are in canonical field range [0, p)
target_description.critical_finding_criteria: Panic on any input, or evaluation producing result outside canonical range

campaign_methodology.seed_corpus_source: Compiled constraint systems from existing test suite

crashes.description: Arithmetic overflow in evaluate_constraint_expr when processing a fuzzed constraint expression tree with specific byte pattern. The overflow occurs during constraint evaluation with extreme field element operands. Non-critical: does not affect proof soundness — the constraint compiler rejects the malformed expression before it reaches the proving pipeline.

campaign_results.notes: Fuzzing campaign terminated early at 18 seconds after discovering a crash. 18k executions at 1k exec/s. One arithmetic overflow found in compiler.rs:921 (evaluate_constraint_expr). The crash is non-critical — it occurs in the constraint expression evaluation path with adversarially crafted input bytes that produce extreme field element operands. The constraint compiler's validation layer rejects such expressions before they reach the proving pipeline. Corpus grew to 271 entries before crash discovery, indicating good structural exploration of constraint expression trees.
